title: CRAP: Worst Since 2000.
speaker: Kevin Paffrath (Meet Kevin)

macro_themes.view: Despite the selloff, details (nuclear inspections, dispute now over unfrozen funds) suggest a deal is closer; until then there is pain.
10y up ~8-10bp to ~5.26-5.27%; rapid rate-of-change spikes historically break something (credit event), but the underlying economy and productivity are holding up.
Extreme fear in breadth and sentiment are buying opportunities leading to a V-shaped recovery over 6-12 months and eventually a real AI bubble top.
Markets price ~68% odds of an October hike; he leans that a 'no' could be the better bet if an Iran deal comes.
Warsh will cut rates rather than print money, which is bearish gold, bullish low-build real estate, and eventually drives the 10y to record lows.

calls.condition: Depends on an Iran deal; "If we don't get a deal, we're all screwed"
calls.reason: DCA buying dips at 700/710/715/735 on QQQ into a hoped-for Iran deal; extreme fear readings signal opportunity; 735 is the key line being rejected.
calls.quote: I'm a big fan of buying this these dips... over the next six to 24 months this will look like a buying opportunity

calls.condition: Needs to hold the trend line
calls.reason: Holding and bouncing off a trend line is what is needed to get Bitcoin up to its 102K level.
calls.quote: That is the bounce you want to see to get Bitcoin up to its 102 level

calls.reason: Gold peaked under Warsh; he will cut rates rather than print money, so the debasement trade does not work.
calls.quote: I personally maintain gold peaked under Worsh and Worsh is not going to be a money printer

calls.reason: Without money printing, disinflation/deflation forces market yields lower than ever, even below what the zero Fed bound implies.
calls.quote: market function 10ear Treasury could go even lower

notes: Micron earnings "tomorrow" and ADP "Wednesday the 30th" => recorded Tue Sep 29. QQQ ~732 at recording. SocGen allocation/consumer-discretionary ideas are attributed to SocGen, not recorded as his calls.
